title: Deep learning epicardial fat measures on cardiac CT predict cardiovascular events
summary: Automated deep learning software quantified epicardial adipose tissue volume and attenuation on noncontrast cardiac CT in 2068 asymptomatic EISNER trial participants. Over 14 +/- 3 years, 223 had major adverse cardiovascular events; higher volume and lower attenuation were independently associated with events, with a hazard ratio of 1.35 (1.07-1.68) for volume. The deep learning step is a measurement tool, and the finding is a prognostic association in one trial cohort.
ai_technology: Fully automated deep learning software for epicardial adipose tissue volume and attenuation on noncontrast cardiac CT

evidence.tested: Prognostic analysis of an existing trial cohort of 2068 asymptomatic subjects with 14-year follow-up, compared with coronary artery calcium and ASCVD risk scores.
evidence.unknown: Whether use of these measures improves clinical decisions or outcomes; replication outside the EISNER cohort; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Segments and quantifies epicardial adipose tissue, which is then related to long-term events.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; first-author affiliations from Crossref. Publisher full text not accessed.
